tips.title: Proper Knife Sharpening for Scale Models
tips.text: For precise cuts, use a diamond stone with a coarse grit (600-800) to sharpen a #11 X-Acto knife. Apply light pressure and maintain a 20° angle. Progress to finer grits (1200-2400) for a high-luster finish. Store the knife in a dry environment to prevent rust.

tips.title: Sawing Techniques for Thin Materials
tips.text: When sawing thin plastics or metals, use a curved-blade hobby saw with a 10-15° bevel. Apply gentle, consistent pressure and use a sawing motion that follows the curve of the blade. This will help prevent binding and maintain a smooth cut.

tips.title: Precision Filing for Smooth Edges
tips.text: For precise edges and smooth surfaces, use a flat-file with a fine tooth count (22-24 TPI). Hold the file at a 30° angle and use a light touch, maintaining consistent pressure. This will help prevent uneven wear and ensure a high-quality finish.

tips.title: Sanding Techniques for Scale Models
tips.text: To achieve a high-gloss finish on scale models, use a flat-sandpaper with a high-grit rating (12000-15000). Apply gentle pressure and use a circular motion, working in small sections. This will help prevent scratches and maintain a smooth surface.

tips.title: Tool Maintenance for Scale Model Tools
tips.text: Regularly inspect and clean your tools, especially after use with abrasive materials. Use a soft-bristled brush to remove debris, and apply a small amount of oil to metal parts to prevent corrosion. This will help maintain tool sharpness and prolong their lifespan.
